about.title: Hawaiian Gardens Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Hawaiian Gardens is a small, tightly packed city in Los Angeles County, and its main corridors — Carson Street, Norwalk Boulevard, Belshire Avenue, and 221st Street — carry a steady flow of local and cut-through traffic. Public crash records show 34 injury collisions and 42 people hurt in the most recent full year, with reports clustering on Friday afternoons between 2 and 4 p.m., a window when work traffic, errands, and school pickups tend to overlap. Whether your crash happened at a busy intersection or on a quieter residential street, the aftermath usually brings the same pressures: medical bills, missed work, and calls from an insurance adjuster asking for a statement. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects injured Hawaiian Gardens residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate the claim and explain the options, without any upfront cost or obligation.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls Back

items.title: California's Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a car accident claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a city vehicle or a road defect — is involved. An attorney can help sort out which deadline applies before evidence disappears.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by whatever percentage of blame gets assigned to you. Insurance adjusters know this and often push recorded statements early to get you to admit something that shifts blame your way.

items.title: No Cap Means Your Story Matters
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so the details of how the crash affected your daily life carry real weight. An attorney working on contingency has an incentive to document that impact fully, since there's no fee unless you recover.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's usually best to hold off until you've spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize or deny your claim later, and anything you say can be taken out of context. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my accident happened at a Hawaiian Gardens intersection with a red light camera or nearby city cameras?
items.answer: Footage from traffic cameras, nearby businesses, or even doorbell cameras along corridors like Carson Street or Norwalk Boulevard can disappear or get overwritten within days or weeks. Preserving that evidence quickly is one of the first things an attorney can help arrange.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after your initial conversation.
